free_tier.stated: 5 GB Git + 20 GB packages + 10 GB Git LFS + 10 GB attachments
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: 500 MB per release asset or issue/comment attachment
per_object_cap.notes: the usage-quotas page caps release assets and issue/comment attachments at 500 MB per file, web-editor uploads at 100 MB, and states no per-file limit for LFS objects and packages

retention.stated: Single small operator on one Hetzner box; nightly off-site backups with 90-day retention described as disaster recovery, not per-account restore
retention.notes: backups are taken on a schedule (repositories hourly, other data daily, database full every Sunday with diff backups on other days) and stored off-site; no retention period is stated

tooling: Full Forgejo API v1 (packages, generic, OCI registry, releases, LFS) + rclone's Gitea/Forgejo-compatible WebDAV-free REST via any HTTP client; OCI via ORAS/skopeo; package registry speaks Generic/Docker/npm/PyPI etc.
chaining: Unlimited free accounts -> 5+20+10+10 = 45 GB of separately-metered pools per identity. Because packages (20 GB) and LFS (10 GB) are separate pools from Git (5 GB), one account yields ~45 GB across four subjects, and each further account carries the same 45 GB. Registry blobs are anonymous-pullable, so shard across repos like any OCI store.
limits_note: Per-account quotas only (5 GB git / 20 GB packages / 10 GB LFS / 10 GB attachments). Download counter booked hourly at the edge proxy; a limit will be set later (currently 429 only after an as-yet-unset threshold). Uploads and Git ops never blocked by traffic limits. 2500 CI minutes/month.

identity_cost.detail: Registration asks for a username, an email address and a password.

reliability_note: Single small operator on one Hetzner box; nightly off-site backups with 90-day retention described as disaster recovery, not per-account restore. Explicit published policy of monitoring several accounts used to exceed its quota and deleting/suspending. The chaining path is actively watched, unlike GitLab's.
